title: Add token metering unit tests for tool calls + structured output paths
author: Leila Farouk
description: Context: We’ve had recurring customer confusion/disputes where billed token attribution diverges between OpenAI-compatible chat/tooling flows vs. non-tooling flows, and we’ve also seen internal drift after small parser changes. This PR adds a focused unit test suite that locks down token metering behavior for (a) tool/function calling and (b) structured output (JSON mode / schema-guided output) so we can safely evolve request parsing + model adapters without accidentally changing billed_tokens attribution. Scope: tests only (no meter logic changes). What’s covered: (1) ChatCompletions tool_calls: assistant emits tool_calls with function name + arguments; verify prompt_tokens vs completion_tokens counts align with our meter spec and stay stable across adapters. (2) Tool role messages: tool result messages included back into the context; verify they are counted as prompt tokens on the next model call, not completion, and that tool “name” fields are handled consistently. (3) Parallel tool calls: multiple tool_calls in a single assistant turn; verify deterministic serialization and that we don’t double-count the tool call wrapper fields. (4) Structured output: response_format=json_schema and json_object modes; verify that schema scaffolding tokens are treated consistently and the emitted JSON is counted only in completion. (5) Regression fixtures for known bug: previously we counted the function.arguments string twice when adapters re-materialized tool messages; the tests would have caught this. Notes: These tests intentionally assert on billed_tokens (not raw tokens) and include a small helper that runs the same cases through the OpenAI-compat layer and native Redwood route to ensure alignment. Related: SUP-28451 (invoice tokens do not match usage export) and ongoing metering hardening work in ENG-4410 / PM-1842. Follow-up: streaming partial-chunk tests live in ENG-4410/ENG-4410 follow-on; this PR keeps unit tests deterministic and fast (<2s).
commits: test(metering): add tool_call metering fixtures for chat completions
test(metering): add structured output (json_schema/json_object) token assertions
test(util): add adapter parity harness (openai-compat vs native request parser)
chore: tighten tokenizer snapshot formatting + add docs in test README
conversation: Nadia Rahman (review): The direction is right. Two nits: (1) Please assert on billed_tokens breakdown (prompt/completion) rather than only total, and (2) ensure the parity harness pins the same model tokenizer config so we don’t get false positives when model defaults shift.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated assertions to check prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, and billed_tokens_total. Also wired the harness to explicitly pass tokenizer_profile='rw-tokenizer-v4' to both paths (native + openai-compat).

Cole Summers (review): Can we add a regression for the double-materialization scenario we saw in SUP-28451? Specifically: adapter builds tool message then downstream re-serializes tool_calls again. That’s where we doubled function.arguments in February.

Leila Farouk (author): Added fixture tool_calls/double_materialization_case.json and a test that simulates the adapter path by passing both tool_calls and an equivalent tool role message; verifies we only count the arguments once. Linked the test comment to SUP-28451 for future archaeology.

Allison Grant (review): Please avoid hardcoding exact token counts for every fixture unless needed; it tends to be brittle across tokenizer profile changes. Prefer invariants where possible (e.g., tool result must be prompt tokens; JSON output must be completion tokens). Where you do pin counts, add a short note explaining why it must remain stable (billing semantics).

Leila Farouk (author): Agreed. Converted most tests to invariants and kept exact token snapshots only for two billing-critical fixtures (simple_tool_call + json_schema_user_profile). Added comments + README section explaining what’s pinned vs invariant and why.

Monica Patel (review): Looks good. Small suggestion: include a case where function.name is non-ASCII / contains hyphens to match what SDKs allow, and make sure serialization doesn’t normalize it unexpectedly.
Leila Farouk (author): Added function name 'search-v2_β' fixture and verified we preserve it in serialization and token attribution. Tests pass.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping these fast/deterministic and for asserting on billed_tokens specifically.
Cole Summers (approval): Approved. This should reduce churn in Finance recon whenever we touch request parsing.
release_notes: Internal: Added unit test coverage to prevent regressions in billed token attribution for tool/function calling and structured output flows (OpenAI-compat + native parity).
